# PLAN — iteration 4
## Current state assessment
The incumbent is timing-feasible at 161 LUTs, 317 FFs, WNS 0.197 ns, and DSP 10. Iterations 2 and 3 were rejected; the latest candidate still must beat the incumbent’s LUT count to improve the `minimize_luts` objective. The current source stores eight 28-bit products and four 28-bit partial sums, although the coefficients are all even and their half-coefficient products need fewer bits.

## Hypothesis
Factoring out the common coefficient factor of two and narrowing each registered product and partial sum to its exact signed range will reduce arithmetic and register logic, potentially lowering LUT use while preserving the five-slot pipeline behavior.

## Instruction for generator
In `fir16_sym_core`, replace the eight full-coefficient product registers with products of the 17-bit pair sums by the half coefficients `-3, -10, -12, 9, 55, 113, 165, 195`, using signed widths of 19, 21, 21, 21, 23, 24, 25, and 25 bits respectively. Narrow the registered grouped sums to 22, 22, 25, and 26 signed bits, sign-extend them into an exact 27-bit half-accumulator, and compute rounding as `(half_acc + 27'sd512) >>> 10`, which is equivalent to the existing full accumulator rounding because the original coefficients are all even. Preserve the five ready-controlled register stages, valid-slot movement, synchronous reset behavior, top `// @latency 5` annotation, and exact saturation and handshake behavior; compare routed LUTs and timing against the 161-LUT feasible incumbent.
